newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka stocks end up, volume led by foreigners.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka stocks end up, volume led by foreigners.

text.p: Sri Lanka stocks closed up as buyers returned on Thursday, with volumes led by foreign purchases of plantation shares, brokers said.
The all share index closed 2.54 points up at 727.90. Price declines led gains by 31 to 21. Ceylon Tobacco rose 1.25 rupees to 41.50, Richard Pieris 2.25 to 105.25.
"Buyers are heading back towards the market because they believe the index had found firm support around the 725 point," said a broker who declined to be identified.
Colombo stocks had been range-trading for almost a week after profit-taking.
Turnover rose sharply to 223.9 million rupees from 77.4 million on Wednesday, led by foreign buying of 3.8 million Bogawantalawa Plantations and 2.07 million Kelani Valley Plantations.
Investment bank Vanik Incorporation said it intended making an offer for the controlling interest in Forbes Ceylon.
Brokers said the announcement led to heavy trading in shares of both corporates.
